report.releaseDate: 22 Oct 2026 (HKEX announcement, 04:00 HKT; LVS release 21 Oct 2026 after US close)
report.currency: USD (Sands China reports in US$; tables in millions unless stated). HK$ items converted at ~7.84 HKD/USD.
report.verdict: A volume-and-share quarter that did not reach the P&L. Sands China grew gaming volumes in every segment (rolling +31%, non-rolling drop +11%, slot/ETG handle +26% YoY) and lifted mass GGR share to 26.1% – its best since Q4-23 – yet luck-adjusted EBITDA of $518m was -13.5% YoY and flat QoQ, because Londoner's premium-mass hold collapsed 480bps and the cost base is now ~$100m/quarter heavier. The reported +23% QoQ EBITDA rebound to $529m is almost entirely hold normalisation; shares fell 4.5% to a fresh 52-week low of HK$10.86 (~$1.39).
summary: **Headline: in line with a de-rated bar, below the published consensus.** SCL net revenue +1.4% YoY to $1.93bn (US GAAP), adj. property EBITDA -12.0% to $529m, net income -29.8% to $191m. JPMorgan put luck-adjusted EBITDA ($518m) ~2% below the $527m sell-side consensus but above buy-side numbers that had drifted sub-$500m; Citi was 4% below its own forecast; CLSA called it 'in line'. The market read it as 'weak but known': 1928.HK -4.5%.

**The QoQ 'rebound' is luck, not operations.** Reported EBITDA rose $99m QoQ ($430m → $529m), but Q2 carried an $87m unfavourable rolling-hold hit and Q3 a $11m favourable one. On a luck-adjusted basis EBITDA was $517m → $518m – flat – and the luck-adjusted margin improved only 30bps to 27.0% (vs 31.5% in Q3-25).

**Which 'division' drove it: The Londoner.** Londoner EBITDA -18.7% YoY to $178m (margin 26.0%, -590bps) on non-rolling hold of 18.6% vs 23.4% – management attributed it to playing 'unlucky' against super-high-end premium-mass customers. At prior-year hold, Londoner's table win would have been ~$135m higher (our estimate, pre-tax/rebates). Every other Cotai property except Venetian grew revenue.

**Volumes and share are genuinely strong.** Portfolio rolling-chip volume $5.74bn (+31% YoY), non-rolling drop $7.18bn (+11%), slot/ETG handle $6.60bn (+26%). Slot/ETG revenue +18% vs +9% for the Macau market. Mass GGR share 26.1% is the best since Q4-23; our rough estimate of share of total market GGR is ~25% (gross win ~$1.9bn vs DICJ Q3 GGR MOP60.2bn/~$7.46bn).

**Market backdrop is deteriorating and management cannot explain the high end.** Macau Q3-26 GGR -3.8% YoY (-1.3% QoQ), mass baccarat -7.9%, VIP flat, slots +18.8%; September (-1.2%) was the fourth consecutive monthly YoY decline and analysts expect October to be the fifth. Management cited macro, the World Cup and Chinese offshore-wealth tax concerns but explicitly could not isolate a cause.

**Cost base is structurally higher and management will not cut it.** Macao Ops opex $1,411m, +$106m (+8.1%) YoY; ~$25m of that is gaming tax on higher win, the remaining ~$80m is table operating hours, sales/marketing/service headcount. Dumont: 'focused on investment for growth, not on cutting our personnel we just hired'. Fixed costs were flat QoQ and no significant further headcount build is planned beyond cost-of-living adjustments.

**Reinvestment is being optimised, not escalated.** Grant Chum said SCL has reduced reinvestment sequentially since Q1 while gaining share; the market 'remains very competitive' with no let-up but no major escalation either. Promo intensity is not disclosed as a % of handle.

**Venetian is the drag by design.** Revenue -6.2% to $649m, EBITDA -15.3% to $205m (31.6% margin) with ~400 rooms out in Q3, ~500 out in Q4 and through Q4-27; average tables -28 units, slots -250 units YoY. ~600 renovated rooms are back and feedback 'surpassed expectations'; full reintroduction with premium gaming salons by CNY 2028.

**Base/mid-mass repositioning is working.** Sands Macao revenue +37.5% ($99m, EBITDA +75%), Parisian +6.0% ($231m) with slot handle +39%, Plaza/Four Seasons +15.5% ($238m, EBITDA $85m, 35.7% margin). Patron count grew double digits, property visitation high-single digits, retail tenant sales +10% YoY.

**No formal guidance; the $700m quarterly EBITDA goal is retained with no date.** Management's near-term markers: Q4 seasonally stronger (Golden Week, NBA Macau week year 2, December), ~500 Venetian rooms out, flat fixed opex. We model Q4-26E EBITDA ~$545-575m hold-normalised (see forecast).

**9M-26: revenue +7.8% to $5.81bn, EBITDA -6.5% to $1.59bn, net income -14.0% to $592m.** Margin 27.2% vs 31.4%. Implied Q1-26 was the strong quarter (EBITDA ~$633m); Q2 ($430m) and Q3 ($529m) show the earnings power has reset to ~$520m luck-adjusted until the premium product cycle completes.

**Capital position adequate but tightening.** Unrestricted cash $1.09bn at 30 Sep; HK$18.10bn (~$2.31bn) undrawn on the 2024 SCL Revolver. Total borrowings were $6.43bn at 30 Jun (IFRS; down from $7.10bn at Dec-25 after $613m revolver repayments) – the 30 Sep debt figure is not disclosed. Our net debt estimate ~$5.3bn, ~2.5x annualised EBITDA.

**Refinancing launched 26 Oct.** SCL is marketing USD senior unsecured notes to redeem the $700m 2.300% 2027s, repay the drawn revolver and fund capex. Replacing a 2.3% coupon in today's market likely adds ~$20m/yr of interest (our estimate); terms unpriced.

**Dividend: HK$0.50 interim (~$0.064/sh, HK$4.05bn/~$516m) was paid on 9 Oct – i.e. after quarter end,** so Q4 net debt will rise. On a HK$1.00 annualised payout (~$1.03bn) the yield is ~9.2% at HK$10.86, but cover from FCF after ~$600-700m capex is thin at the current ~$2.1bn EBITDA run-rate.

**LVS keeps buying the subsidiary.** LVS bought 62m SCL shares for HK$793m (~$101m) in Q3, lifting its stake to 75.56%; management reiterated it prefers buying LVS/SCL stock to M&A and has no interest in taking LVS private. Free float continues to shrink.

**Capex framework clarified.** D&A runs ~$750-800m/yr; maintenance capex ~$300m. 2027 development capex centres on three projects: Venetian renovation (highest ROI), Conrad renovation/rebrand into a Londoner-themed hotel, and an accelerated Botanic Garden concession commitment. Q3 Macao capex $154m.

**Income statement below EBITDA:** D&A $197m (+3%), corporate $55m, net interest $73m (vs $76m), SBC $4m, tax $1m. Net income QoQ +78.5% from Q2's $107m. SCL does not report quarterly EPS; implied ~US$0.024 (~HK$0.18) on ~8.09bn shares (our estimate).

**Thesis read-through.** The bull case (share gains + product cycle → operating leverage into $700m/qtr) is intact on volumes but pushed out; the bear case (structurally higher opex into a shrinking, promotionally intense market with an unexplained high-end slowdown) has the near-term numbers. Until the market returns to growth, luck-adjusted EBITDA of ~$520m/qtr and ~27% margin is the base case.

segments.name: Macao gaming operations (by property)
segments.headline: Volumes up across every segment and mass share at a three-year high, but Londoner's 18.6% premium-mass hold and a heavier cost base left luck-adjusted EBITDA flat QoQ at ~$518m.
narrative: They delivered $529m of Macao adjusted property EBITDA on $1.94bn of segment revenue, a 27.3% margin against 31.5% a year ago and 24.0% in Q2. Casino revenue was $1,454m, +1.7% YoY and +10.4% QoQ, on gross table-and-slot win that we estimate at ~$1.90bn (+3.4% YoY, +6.2% QoQ, computed from reported volumes and hold). Rolling-chip volume of $5.74bn was up 31% YoY (though down 24% from Q2's unusually high $7.57bn), non-rolling drop of $7.18bn was +11% YoY and flat QoQ, and slot/ETG handle of $6.60bn was +26% YoY. Management framed the quarter as proof that product, longer table hours, more sales and service staff and an optimised reinvestment programme are winning share – mass GGR share reached 26.1%, the strongest since Q4-23 – while conceding that spend per visitor softened at the high end and that they could not pin down why.

The hold story cuts both ways. Blended rolling hold was 3.64% against the 3.3% expectation, which the company says flattered EBITDA by $11m (revenue by $19m); luck-adjusted EBITDA was therefore $518m, down 13.5% from $599m a year ago and essentially unchanged from Q2's $517m. But management does not hold-adjust the mass business, and that is where the damage sat: blended non-rolling hold fell to 20.4% from 23.1% in Q3-25, driven by The Londoner at 18.6% versus 23.4%, which Grant Chum attributed to playing unlucky against super-high-end premium-mass players. Mass table win across the portfolio was therefore down ~2% YoY despite drop up 11%; had Londoner simply held at last year's rate its table win would have been ~$135m higher on our arithmetic (pre-gaming-tax and rebates), which more than explains the YoY EBITDA shortfall. Slot win rose ~18% to ~$223m, matching the company's statement that slot/ETG revenue grew 18% versus 9% for the market.

The Londoner carried the quarter's weakness: revenue flat at $685m, EBITDA -18.7% to $178m, margin 26.0% (-590bps YoY, -100bps QoQ), even as rolling volume rose 39% to $3.22bn and non-rolling drop rose 24% to $2.80bn; table win per unit per day eased to $12,929 from $13,115 while slot win per unit rose 20% to $696. The Venetian was weak by design – revenue -6.2% to $649m and EBITDA -15.3% to $205m (31.6% margin) with roughly 400 rooms out for renovation in Q3, 28 fewer tables and ~250 fewer slots on the floor; rolling volume still rose 44% to $917m and management flagged a sequential improvement in mass revenue as ~600 renovated rooms returned. The Plaza/Four Seasons swung from a Q2 of negative rolling hold (-1.15%) to 3.76%, lifting revenue 74% QoQ and 15.5% YoY to $238m and EBITDA to $85m (35.7% margin) on rolling volume +13% and non-rolling drop +15%; RevPAR there reached $485 at 96.1% occupancy. The Parisian grew revenue 6% to $231m with slot handle +39% to $1.40bn but EBITDA fell 13% to $46m (19.9% margin, -440bps), and Sands Macao was the standout grower at +37.5% revenue to $99m and EBITDA $14m (+75%) after its slot floor was expanded from 810 to 1,362 units (handle +150% to $1.57bn), albeit at a 2.1% hold.

Cost is now the swing factor. Segment operating costs (revenue less EBITDA) were $1,411m, up $106m or 8.1% YoY and $51m QoQ. We attribute ~$25m of the YoY increase to gaming tax on higher gross win and the remaining ~$80m to the deliberate investment in table operating hours, sales, marketing and customer-service headcount that management first flagged in Q2. The sequential increase is consistent with management's assertion that fixed expenses were essentially flat QoQ, the recent staffing already being embedded in Q2, and that no further significant headcount build is planned beyond cost-of-living adjustments. Dumont was unambiguous that they will not reverse the hiring even if the market stays soft, arguing the teams are needed to operate the renovated premium product as it comes online; Chum added that reinvestment has been reduced sequentially since Q1 while share rose, that the market remains very competitive with no let-up but no major escalation, and that industry-wide moderation will be a function of market revenue growth. Citi read the 30bps luck-adjusted margin improvement as evidence of discipline; we read it as the floor of a cost base that now needs ~$100m/quarter more revenue than a year ago just to stand still.

Capacity and product plans were reiterated rather than changed. The Venetian renovation, started in March, keeps ~500 rooms out of inventory on average through Q4-27 (slightly more than the ~400 out in Q3 as multi-bay Paiza suites are tackled), with the property to be refreshed and reintroduced by Chinese New Year 2028 together with new premium gaming salons. The Conrad will be renovated and rebranded as a Londoner-themed hotel and the Botanic Garden concession project is being accelerated. The portfolio's average table count was unchanged at 1,637 while slots were broadly flat at ~5,500, so near-term growth has to come from yield, share and the return of Venetian rooms rather than capacity. Management retained its goal of $700m of quarterly EBITDA – a 35% uplift on the current luck-adjusted run-rate – explicitly conditional on completing the product programme and on the Macau market growing again; no timeline was given.

On the market, Q3 Macau GGR fell 3.8% YoY to MOP60.2bn (~$7.46bn), down 1.3% QoQ, with mass baccarat -7.9%, the broader mass segment -5.2%, VIP +0.1% and slots +18.8%; September's -1.2% was the fourth consecutive monthly decline and the lowest monthly total of 2026, and analysts on the call suggested October will be the fifth. Chum said the decline was sharper in June and July than in August and September (the World Cup effect) and that Q4 is seasonally stronger (Golden Week extended by the NBA Macau games, then December) 'all else equal', while declining to say how the current contraction plays through. JPMorgan estimates industry Q3 EBITDA fell ~10% YoY and sees downside risk to 2H26/2027 estimates. Against that, SCL's double-digit patron growth, high-single-digit visitation growth and 10% retail tenant-sales growth argue its share gains are real; the question is the value of share in a shrinking, promotionally intense market.

segments.name: Non-gaming: hotel, retail mall, F&B and ferry
segments.headline: Non-gaming held up – rooms flat on fewer keys, Cotai malls at an 87% operating margin with tenant sales +10% – but ferry/other EBITDA fell to $1m.
narrative: They generated $486m of non-casino revenue in the quarter (25% of segment revenue), essentially flat YoY (+2.0%) on a hotel base shrunk by the Venetian renovation. Room revenue of $214m was down 2.7% YoY because of the ~400 Venetian rooms out of service, but every property ran at or above 96% occupancy and rate held: Venetian ADR $200 (RevPAR $197), Londoner $264 ($257, +$4), Plaza/Four Seasons $504 ($485, +$29 on occupancy +350bps to 96.1%), Parisian $144 ($142, -$5) and Sands Macao $162 ($161). The Londoner hotel complex was the room-revenue engine at $103m, and management noted the premium-suite inventory returning at the Venetian (~600 rooms) is being managed for customer mix rather than volume, which is the right call while table hold is doing the damage elsewhere.

Retail remains the highest-quality earnings stream in the portfolio. Cotai mall gross revenue was $131m in the quarter with operating profit of $114m, an 87.0% margin, on 1.87m sq ft of GLA at 87.3% occupancy and trailing-twelve-month tenant sales of $2,349/sq ft. The Shoppes at Venetian contributed $63m revenue/$56m profit at 94.1% occupancy and $2,201/sq ft; the Shoppes at Four Seasons $37m/$33m with luxury retail at 100% occupancy and $5,614/sq ft; the Shoppes at Londoner $26m/$22m but still only 82.4% let; and the Shoppes at Parisian $5m/$3m at 69.5% occupancy and $421/sq ft, which remains the portfolio's weak corner. Chum highlighted that tenant sales grew 10% YoY despite the weaker China consumption backdrop, with strength in both luxury and mass retail – a useful cross-check that visitation and wallet are intact even as high-end gaming spend softened. Segment mall revenue in the P&L was $133m (+2.3% YoY).

Food & beverage revenue rose 2.9% to $72m and convention/retail/other rose 16% to $29m, with the Londoner adding $3m in each of F&B, mall and convention lines YoY – consistent with the NBA Cares/community week and MICE activations that management described as even more successful in year two. Ferry operations and other revenue grew 19% to $38m but EBITDA dropped to $1m from $5m (2.6% margin versus 15.6%), and 9M ferry/other EBITDA is $8m against $18m; the company did not explain the deterioration and it is small, but it is a $16m-a-year leak worth a question at the next call.

Non-gaming will matter more as the capital programme lands. The Venetian reintroduction by CNY 2028 brings back ~500 renovated keys skewed to suites and Paiza product, the Conrad becomes a Londoner-branded hotel, and the accelerated Botanic Garden fulfils a concession commitment that the government weighs in its assessment of concessionaires. None of these add gaming capacity; their payoff is premium room nights and the gaming yield attached to them, which is precisely the segment that went quiet this quarter.

segments.name: Balance sheet, capital returns and development pipeline
segments.headline: Liquidity is comfortable ($1.09bn cash, ~$2.31bn undrawn revolver, 2027 notes being refinanced), but a ~$1bn annual dividend against ~$2.1bn run-rate EBITDA and a multi-year capex cycle leaves little slack if the market keeps contracting.
narrative: They ended September with $1.09bn of unrestricted cash (US GAAP) and HK$18.10bn (~$2.31bn) of availability under the 2024 SCL Revolving Facility. The Q3 announcement does not disclose period-end debt; the last reported figure is total borrowings of $6.43bn at 30 June 2026 under IFRS, down from $7.10bn at December 2025 after $613m of revolver repayments in Q2. Taking that June debt figure against September cash gives an indicative net debt of ~$5.3bn, roughly 2.5x annualised 9M EBITDA of ~$2.1bn and ~3.0x gross – manageable for an investment-grade-adjacent Macau concessionaire, but trending the wrong way given the $516m interim dividend that left the balance sheet on 9 October, after quarter-end.

On 26 October SCL launched an offering of USD senior unsecured notes (Rule 144A/Reg S, professional investors only) to redeem in full the $700m 2.300% notes due 2027 with accrued interest, repay the drawn balance on the 2024 revolver and fund general corporate purposes including capex. Size and coupon are unpriced; refinancing a 2.3% coupon at prevailing levels implies incremental interest in the order of $20m a year on our estimate, which is a modest but real drag on the ~$290m annual net interest line (9M net interest $225m, down 7.8% YoY on lower average debt and rates). Net interest in Q3 was $73m against $76m a year ago.

Capital returns are being set by the parent's needs as much as the subsidiary's. SCL doubled its interim dividend to HK$0.50 per share (HK$4.05bn/~$516m) in August, which with the FY25 final implies an annualised HK$1.00 (~$1.03bn) payout and a ~9.2% yield at HK$10.86 – the single most-cited support in the Citi and JPMorgan notes. Against that, EBITDA of ~$2.1bn less ~$290m interest, negligible cash tax and capex that management frames as ~$300m maintenance plus a development programme (Venetian, Conrad, Botanic Garden) leaves free cash flow after capex around $1.1-1.2bn on our arithmetic, so the dividend is covered but with little room for a further step-down in EBITDA. LVS meanwhile bought another 62m SCL shares for HK$793m (~$101m) in Q3, lifting its stake to 75.56%; Dumont said capital will go to LVS and SCL buybacks rather than M&A and that there is no interest in taking LVS private. The free float keeps shrinking, which supports the share technically but makes the dividend a parent-level funding decision.

The capex frame given on the call is the most useful new disclosure: D&A runs $750-800m a year, maintenance capex is ~$300m, and 2027 development capex comprises the Venetian renovation (the highest-ROI project, completion by CNY 2028), the Conrad renovation and rebrand into a Londoner-themed hotel, and the accelerated Botanic Garden concession project. Q3 Macao capex was $154m. Our read is that total capex runs $600-700m a year through 2027, after which the Venetian programme rolls off; the earnings payoff is back-end loaded into 2028 and depends on the premium segment that went quiet this quarter returning.

blocks.heading: Liquidity and leverage
blocks.takeaway: Liquidity is comfortable with $1.09bn cash and ~$2.31bn undrawn revolver, but indicative net debt of ~$5.3bn is trending the wrong way.
points: Unrestricted cash $1.09bn (US GAAP); HK$18.10bn (~$2.31bn) available under the 2024 SCL Revolving Facility.
Period-end debt not disclosed; last reported total borrowings $6.43bn at 30 June 2026 (IFRS), down from $7.10bn at December 2025 after $613m of Q2 revolver repayments.
Net debt ~$5.3bn is roughly 2.5x annualised 9M EBITDA of ~$2.1bn and ~3.0x gross, manageable for an investment-grade-adjacent concessionaire.
The $516m interim dividend left the balance sheet on 9 October, after quarter-end.

blocks.heading: Refinancing
blocks.takeaway: SCL launched USD senior unsecured notes on 26 October to redeem the $700m 2.300% 2027 notes; we estimate ~$20m a year of incremental interest.
points: Offering is Rule 144A/Reg S to professional investors; proceeds also repay the drawn 2024 revolver and fund general corporate purposes including capex.
Size and coupon are unpriced.
Annual net interest line is ~$290m; 9M net interest $225m, down 7.8% YoY on lower average debt and rates.
Q3 net interest $73m against $76m a year ago.

blocks.heading: Capital returns
blocks.takeaway: Annualised dividend of HK$1.00 (~$1.03bn), a ~9.2% yield at HK$10.86, is covered by ~$1.1-1.2bn free cash flow but with little room for EBITDA to fall further.
points: Interim dividend doubled to HK$0.50 per share (HK$4.05bn/~$516m) in August; the yield is the single most-cited support in Citi and JPMorgan notes.
Free cash flow arithmetic: EBITDA ~$2.1bn less ~$290m interest, negligible cash tax, ~$300m maintenance capex plus development programme.
LVS bought another 62m SCL shares for HK$793m (~$101m) in Q3, lifting its stake to 75.56%.
Dumont said capital will go to LVS and SCL buybacks rather than M&A, with no interest in taking LVS private.
Shrinking free float supports the share technically but makes the dividend a parent-level funding decision.

blocks.heading: Capex and pipeline
blocks.takeaway: We read total capex at $600-700m a year through 2027, with earnings payoff back-end loaded into 2028 and dependent on premium demand returning.
points: D&A runs $750-800m a year; maintenance capex ~$300m; Q3 Macao capex was $154m.
2027 development capex comprises the Venetian renovation (highest-ROI project, completion by CNY 2028), the Conrad rebrand into a Londoner-themed hotel and the accelerated Botanic Garden project.
The Venetian programme rolls off after 2027.

highlights.text: Volume growth in every segment – rolling +31%, non-rolling drop +11%, slot/ETG handle +26% YoY – with mass GGR share at 26.1%, the highest since Q4-23, in a market where mass GGR fell 5.2%. Patron count up double digits, visitation up high-single digits.

Slot/ETG revenue +18% versus +9% for the market, and the base/mid-mass properties are compounding: Sands Macao revenue +37.5% (EBITDA +75%), Parisian +6% with slot handle +39%, Plaza/Four Seasons +15.5% with a 35.7% margin.

Luck-adjusted margin improved 30bps QoQ to 27.0% with reinvestment reduced sequentially while share rose; fixed opex flat QoQ and management says no further significant headcount build – the cost base may have peaked.

Venetian renovation on schedule for CNY 2028; ~600 renovated rooms returned with customer feedback 'surpassing expectations' and mass revenue improving sequentially at the property despite ~400 rooms out.
Retail is a high-quality cushion: Cotai mall operating profit $114m on $131m revenue (87% margin), tenant sales +10% YoY across luxury and mass, Four Seasons luxury retail 100% let at $5,614/sq ft.
Liquidity and funding in hand: $1.09bn cash, ~$2.31bn undrawn revolver, the only near-term maturity ($700m 2027 notes) being refinanced now; LVS continues to buy SCL stock (75.56%).
Rolling hold of 3.64% (vs 3.3% expected) and Plaza/Four Seasons' swing from -1.15% to 3.76% hold added ~$11m of EBITDA and most of the +$99m QoQ headline improvement.

lowlights.text: Luck-adjusted EBITDA $518m, -13.5% YoY and flat QoQ; luck-adjusted margin 27.0% vs 31.5% a year ago. The reported +23% QoQ EBITDA move is hold normalisation, not operating improvement.

Londoner non-rolling hold 18.6% (-480bps YoY) on super-high-end premium-mass play – ~$135m of gross table win forgone on our arithmetic; Londoner EBITDA -18.7% to $178m, margin 26.0%. Unlucky, but it exposes how concentrated the property's mix has become.

Opex +$106m (+8.1%) YoY to $1.41bn, of which ~$80m is deliberate staffing/table-hours/service investment; management explicitly refuses to trim it while the market contracts, so flow-through stays poor until revenue recovers.

Macau market: Q3 GGR -3.8% YoY, mass baccarat -7.9%, four consecutive months of YoY decline with October likely the fifth; management could not identify the cause of high-end softness (macro, World Cup, offshore-wealth tax all cited). JPMorgan flags downside risk to 2H26/2027 industry estimates.
Venetian: revenue -6.2%, EBITDA -15.3%, 28 fewer tables and ~250 fewer slots, ~500 rooms out through Q4-27 – the flagship is a drag for five more quarters.

Net income -29.8% to $191m; implied quarterly EPS ~US$0.024 (~HK$0.18). Dividend cover is thin: ~$1.03bn annualised payout versus ~$1.1-1.2bn FCF after capex at the current ~$2.1bn EBITDA run-rate, and the $516m interim left the balance sheet on 9 Oct.
Ferry & other EBITDA $1m vs $5m (9M $8m vs $18m) and Parisian margin 19.9% (-440bps) – small, unexplained and persistent margin leaks.

Governance/float: LVS at 75.56% and rising, dividend policy effectively set by the parent's capital-return programme; Macau government's 2026 GGR budget (MOP236bn) now needs an implausible ~MOP48bn Q4 – a cut would weigh on sentiment.

forecast.intro: Sands China gives no formal guidance; the only numeric target is the long-standing $700m quarterly EBITDA goal, which was retained without a date and is now explicitly conditional on both completing the product programme and the Macau market growing again. What did change versus Q2 is the operating frame: fixed opex is now flat QoQ with no further headcount build, reinvestment is being reduced sequentially, ~500 Venetian rooms (vs ~400) will be out in Q4, 2027 capex is anchored on three named projects, and the 2027 notes are being refinanced. The YoY EBITDA bridge below shows the quarter was lost at The Londoner's premium-mass tables and in the cost base, not in volumes.

forecast.view: **Q4-26E (our estimates): segment revenue ~$1.98-2.05bn (+2-5% QoQ) and adj. property EBITDA ~$545-575m hold-normalised (margin ~27.5-28%).** Seasonality (Golden Week extended by NBA Macau week year two, December) and a flat fixed-cost base should give modest operating leverage even if market GGR is down low-single digits YoY; the swing factors are Londoner mass hold reverting toward 21-23% (worth ~$60-120m of gross win QoQ) and whether the high-end absence persists. **FY26E EBITDA ~$2.14-2.17bn** (9M $1.59bn + Q4E), margin ~27.3% – a reset from the 31%+ margins of 2025. **2027:** we would not underwrite a return to $600m+/quarter until the Venetian suites and salons are back (CNY 2028); the realistic 2027 range is $2.2-2.4bn, with the $700m/quarter goal a 2028+ event. **Leverage drifts up, not down:** the $516m interim dividend paid 9 Oct plus ~$150-200m quarterly capex against ~$300m of EBITDA-less-interest-less-capex means Q4 net debt rises toward ~$5.6-5.8bn (our estimate, ~2.6-2.7x), and the new notes will carry a materially higher coupon than the 2.3% they replace. Dividend sustainability at HK$1.00/yr hinges on EBITDA holding ~$2.1bn; a FY25-style final of HK$0.50 in February is our base case but the margin of safety is thin.
watch: Macau October GGR print (early November) – a fifth consecutive YoY decline and any government cut to the MOP236bn 2026 budget assumption.
Londoner non-rolling hold in Q4 (reverting toward 21-23%?) and whether super-premium visitation returns post Golden Week/NBA week.
Pricing and size of the new USD senior notes and the resulting net interest run-rate; disclosure of 30 Sep net debt in the FY26 results.
Q4 Macao opex: management promised flat fixed costs – any further increase breaks the 'peak cost base' thesis.
Venetian: ~500 rooms out in Q4; sequential mass revenue and premium salon progress; any slippage versus CNY 2028.
FY25-style final dividend decision (February 2027) and LVS's continued SCL share purchases/free-float implications.
Competitive reinvestment intensity (Galaxy, MGM China, Melco, Wynn, SJM) – management sees 'no let-up but no escalation'; a step-up would hit margin directly.
Policy: Chinese offshore-wealth tax enforcement and visa/travel measures affecting premium-mass and rolling demand.
